page: Microsoft Azure FX24mds is a high-memory compute instance designed for demanding workloads requiring a substantial memory-to-core ratio alongside dedicated processing resources. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the virtual machine is powered by an x86_64 Intel processor configured with 24 dedicated vCPUs. The server balances focused core execution with a large memory allocation, provisioning 504.0 GB of system RAM, which calculates to 21.0 GB of memory per individual vCPU.

Storage configuration includes a 1082 GB local solid-state drive (SSD) for temporary or scratch data, supplemented by support for Azure Premium Storage. The hardware profile does not include graphics accelerators, maintaining a GPU count of zero. Networking allocation includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard virtual network configuration for external connectivity.

With 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, the instance delivers high resource density for memory-bound tasks. This architecture reduces resource contention by avoiding shared-thread penalties via dedicated vCPU mapping. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of discrete GPU acceleration, focusing entirely on high-capacity memory retention and central processing.

Workload suitability centers on enterprise-scale in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational database management systems requiring significant buffer pool capacities, large batch data processing, and stateful analytical engines.
